prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: Frames 1–2 show a room boundary: a dark doorway or curtained opening on the left, furniture immediately below it, and a broad wall extending across the centre and right; the opening/furniture appears roughly 2–4 m away, while the wall is about 1–3 m away. In frame 3 the camera turns or moves toward the right-hand wall, which fills most of the view at approximately 0.5–1.5 m, with darker, more distant space remaining at left and low furniture or clutter near the bottom. In frames 4–5 a large body part or similarly close foreground form crosses the upper-right/centre, probably within 0.2–0.7 m, occluding much of the room; nearby floor-level objects remain partly visible below it, while the far wall stays behind. The depth map makes near/far layering and the rapid approach of the foreground surface clearer than RGB, but its smooth halos, weak object boundaries, saturated bright regions, and changing brightness make metre estimates and distances between individual objects unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map is entirely black in all five frames, so it identifies no people, body parts, furniture, walls, or other object instances and supplies no inter-object distances or relative positions. Consequently it does not resolve the doorway and furniture visible on the left in frames 1–2, the close wall in frame 3, or the foreground body-like form and partial floor clutter in frames 4–5. It also provides no evidence about facing direction, gaze, reachability, occlusion ownership, or approach and retreat across time. Its all-black output is unreliable for this sequence, likely representing complete detection or rendering failure rather than an empty scene.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is entirely black across all five frames, with no yellow body skeletons or magenta hand skeletons detected. It therefore provides no spatial evidence about how many people are present, where bodies or hands lie, which way anyone faces, whether anyone looks toward the camera, or what lies within any person's arm's reach. In particular, it cannot determine whether the close form crossing frames 4–5 belongs to the camera wearer or another person, and it does not expose joints hidden by that foreground occlusion or by the image boundaries. No turning, approach, retreat, or limb motion can be measured from this map, so the absent pose output is unreliable despite body-like content in the RGB strip.
